summary: FBRX 2.5.0 Beta (Weft): the FBRX apps with FBRX Digger for the advanced network tools, remote screen to your own computers and from FBRX Command, the FBRX directory, Devices in This PC, and the Lab in every edition.
notes: FBRX apps (Settings → FBRX apps): FBRX Digger is the network toolkit, with Ultra. Scans, consoles, network environments and adapter settings move there; the Network Center keeps the full network check, Wi-Fi, speed, Bluetooth and printers, and its Digger tab opens Digger or offers the download. Fabrix runs the everyday checks itself and offers Open Digger or Get Digger for more.

Remote screen (Pro): see or use your other computers over FBRX Mesh. The person there says yes each time, unless you let one of your own computers in without asking, and a red bar with Stop shows while it lasts.
FBRX Command's administrators can see or use a computer's screen for support, with a ticket number and the person's yes; organizations can keep recordings, and the person is told before answering.
Remote desktop on Linux (Settings → Remote desktop, Pro): sets up the system's own remote desktop so any RDP app can sign in, also on a server with nobody at it.

The FBRX directory: the same accounts, groups, administrators and password rules on every computer that joins an FBRX Server (Settings → Directory). Changes are applied through the system's own administrator prompt.

This PC → Devices (Pro): screens, graphics cards, external drives with Eject and a speed test, the USB tree with the speed each device runs at, printers with their ink and toner, and screen brightness, contrast and input.

The Lab in every edition: in Essentials, Show the Lab (Settings → General) adds the Terminal with the command line and FBRX/1; from Pro the Lab is in the menu with the device consoles. Organizations can turn the Terminal off.
Learning your computer: after setup and when you pick a new AI model, FBRX gets the AI ready with what it needs to know about this computer, so the first answer comes ready.
Mesh is in Pro, and Black Hole Edition can be bought by one person, not only an organization.
Fabrix never sees your saved passwords, keeps the right tools at hand in long chats, says plainly what it cannot do, and can quote Bible verses word for word, offline.
The Black Hole theme, and Bruce the Goose, who now plays hide-and-seek inside the FBRX window.
FBRX Shield's threat feed uses abuse.ch's keyed export (a free key, in Credentials); the abuse.ch key is only ever sent to abuse.ch.

server.summary: FBRX Server 1.4.5: Bridge a port from the console, FBRX Time copies off the server, Ubuntu quick downloads in the ISO library, thin or thick VM disks, and long pastes into a VM that arrive as typed.
notes: Networks → Bridge a port… (administrators): makes bridge br0 on one of the server's ports (its DHCP or fixed address moves to the bridge, or a spare card), says what an outer hypervisor (VMware, Hyper-V, VirtualBox) must allow, and Restart now finishes it.
FBRX Time: a copy of each new image off the server, to a NAS share, an NFS export or a USB drive, tested before it is saved and changeable any time.
ISO library: quick downloads of Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Desktop and Server, the newest point release, checked against Ubuntu's checksums.
New VMs: thin or thick provisioned disks.
Long pastes into a VM's console arrive as typed.
From 1.1: sudo fbrx-server update check, then sudo fbrx-server update commit.

digger.summary: FBRX Digger 1.3.0: the network toolkit of the FBRX apps, with Ultra, taking over FBRX Endpoint's advanced network tools and its saved connections.
notes: Digger runs at the edition FBRX Endpoint's license gives this computer, and needs Ultra.
Your saved connections and network environments come over from FBRX Endpoint once, without passwords or keys.
Fabrix in Digger has the scan, console and environment tools that moved here.
